answer: A falcon-fast registry resists sybils by requiring each agent to lock a decaying bond in escrow before acting: the bond is released only after a violet audit window in which a rotating beacon committee re-checks the agent's claimed work against its public history. Clones share one bond pool, so spawning N identities splits the same stake N ways and each clone's slashable share falls below the profit threshold, while an honest agent recovers its full bond plus a small fee. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count, but legitimate entry stays cheap for a single identity.
